projects.name: Genius AI
projects.status: Shipped to production — strategy, roadmap and release
projects.role: Senior Product Manager — product strategy and roadmap
projects.summary: The AI layer inside Genius, the Global Payments POS — product strategy, roadmap, and the platform bet underneath both.
projects.description: The AI layer of the Genius point-of-sale. Owns what earns funding, what gets built first, and where the platform boundary sits. The defining bet: scope the agent core, evaluation approach and guardrails once and reuse them across Genius POS rather than rebuilding per segment, so a new surface becomes a configuration problem rather than a new product. Conversational reporting was the first capability to reach operators: concept to production in three months, now resolving 86% of operator questions directly with a 73% merchant return rate. Golden sets and the evals that matter for each use case are the release gate. The team continues to build against the same direction.
projects.note: Quality and engagement rates are published; absolute volumes, revenue and account counts are non-public employer data and are intentionally omitted.
highlights: Concept to production in 3 months; golden sets and the evals that matter for each use case as the release gate
In production: 86% of operator questions resolved directly, 73% merchant return rate
Secured approximately $2M to fund the build
Owns the product roadmap the team continues to build against
Platform-vs-point-solution bet: agent core and evaluation reused across Genius POS, not rebuilt per segment
Conversational reporting as the first capability to reach operators
Evaluation gates as the release decision rather than a compliance step

projects.name: AI-First Voice Ordering
projects.role: Senior Product Manager — thesis, segment economics, POC direction
projects.summary: Voice-first order capture on a Genius handheld, and the product case for where voice is worth building.
projects.description: A server takes a table's order conversationally instead of tapping through screens. The hard product problem is not transcription — it is attributing who said what across several people at one table and applying a mid-order change to the right guest's order. The thesis covers which segments voice genuinely wins in versus where the category is commoditizing, build-vs-buy-vs-partner per lane, and a beachhead channel sequence that proves the agent core under real conditions before committing spend to the next channel.
highlights: Segment selection and channel sequencing that de-risks a multi-channel investment case
Build-vs-buy-vs-partner evaluation per lane
Pricing derived from measured product economics
Dialog confidence policy: when the system captures silently, flags, or asks
Set the quality bar: 500ms p50 voice-to-screen, 90% speaker attribution under overlapping speech, 1.5x word-error ratio across accent subgroups
Speech-to-speech POC directed with engineering and a cloud partner; demoed live to customers

projects.name: Agentic Commerce & Agent Reputation
projects.summary: Why reputation, not identity, is the missing layer in agent-to-agent commerce.
projects.description: Agents are beginning to transact on people's behalf, and the infrastructure has converged quickly on identity: the protocols can answer who an agent is. Almost nothing answers whether it is any good — whether it honors terms, whether its last counterparty would deal with it again. Reputation is what actually gates letting an agent spend someone's money, and the first credible reputation layer carries strong network effects.
highlights: Identity is converging across agent protocols and card-network standards; reputation is not
Reputation as the gating layer for agent-initiated payments
Mechanism design and repeated-game conditions under which agent cooperation holds
Same trust question as the day job, at network scale rather than one operator's

projects.name: Consequence-Weighted AI Evaluation

projects.description: Shifted evaluation focus from standard accuracy metrics to business-impact-adjusted models, identifying high-consequence edge cases early in the development lifecycle.
